utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: No. I'm telling you not in Saborsko but when we returned from Saborsko. Over there in Licka Jesenica. That's when I saw the commander of my battalion, Cedo Bulat, and some other officers, other officers who had ranks.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was any Croat killed in Saborsko? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I know that. That is the first thing I came to know. When we were that first position that I mentioned. The first thing that this group of mine came to know was that there were dead people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What kind of information was that and what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Behind this group of mine that was sort of deployed there, there was another group behind us near the woods, and then from that group, a man came by and he was crying. Tears were rolling down his cheeks, and he said, "They killed Pero Krtan." Pero Krtan was a merchant, an honest man, in my opinion. That's the first thing I came to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who else was killed? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: We heard that there were two men with him, that they were killed and that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know who killed them?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I did not see that, but rumour has it - I don't know if I have to mention the name --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If it is only rumour, no. Thank you. How many people -- how many Croats were killed on that -- during this attack? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know. I thought that with the shelling and artillery and -- I don't know what else. Well, we had some information that about 20 persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was your unit involved in the burying of the bodies of these killed people?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: This was in the area of responsibility of my battalion, but, no. It was people from the brigade, older people in their 60s who went -- well, this was called -- well, these -- this company of older people. They went to bury the dead and also the animals.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was an excavator used for doing this?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, I had to provide fuel. My battalion was supposed to provide fuel for its operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the attack, did you see any of the police commanders that you mentioned, that is Medakovic, Latas, Ogrizovic? Did you see them on that day during the attack?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Not on that day. I did not see them. Well, I mean -- well, not there. I mean, they were on the other side, that's why.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What do you mean they were -- on which other side were they?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: We were to the east, and I later found out that this police was operating down south. So we were pretty far away if you look at the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Saborsko -- what happened to the villagers, the Croat population of Saborsko? Do you know? You said you didn't see them, just a few old people.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: They were collected and brought to this neighbouring Serb village. That's where they were put up. They were given tea, sandwiches, and the next day, they were dispatched onto buses. There were about 50 to 60 of these elderly people there, and they were brought to that line by Ogulin, and they were allowed to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "line," do you mean this line that you describe between the Serbs and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, but the other side, towards Ogulin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Saborsko the only Croat village in the region? Were there others?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, it's the first one on that side. I mean, it's the first Croat village. And then there's this other very small one and then there's Rakovica, Slunj. These are places that are surrounded, but they are Croat places. And then the rest are Serb areas. So these are three places -- well, sort of biggish, but I mean, they are villages, basically. Perhaps Slunj is a bit bigger, but yes, there bigger places.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened to these Croat villages?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Slunj, Rakovica, they all fell ultimately. And then from Knin to Belgrade, the entire area was Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you travel through this region? And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I did not travel then in those parts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, could you please bear in mind the fact that it is five minutes past one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. C-1220, could you please explain something to me. Let us clarify something about Saborsko. You said that Saborsko was a major stronghold of the Croat forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, well, based on assumptions, based on what these officers said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As for the rest that you've been saying, that's not based on assumptions; namely that because of that stronghold, your municipality was under blockade. And also the larger part of the territory on the other side of Saborsko, if I understood it correctly, and you did not have any possibility to communicate further on towards other parts of Krajina or, rather, you said that you could not even obtain supplies and that you were running out of everything. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- it is my understanding on the basis of what you've been saying during your examination-in-chief that the army asked the Croat forces in Saborsko to have free passage along this road and that no one would be in harm's way and that nobody would be attacked or jeopardised.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. These sort of authorities at that time in Plaski, that's what people said. Everybody talked about that. And this offer was made several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they did not want to allow for these communications to be linked up?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in your municipality - I tried to write down what you said - you had shortages of all kinds, even of salt let alone anything else.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, because we could not go anywhere. We were cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were under a total blockade?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that this unit of the army that happened to be there and the training facility that you referred to, et cetera, that they were also under blockade?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, they were in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean since, as you had put it, several times they proposed to the Croat forces to allow free passage along the road and they did not allow that, that it was then necessary to deblockade the road or, rather, to eliminate this stronghold in Saborsko in order to deblockade the road?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Your answer was yes?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there any other way of deblocking the road? Was there another road that could ensure supplies and that made it possible to communicate?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, there were forest paths, but it's impossible to pass that way. And that was not under anybody's control. This was never safe. Do you see what I'm saying? Nobody can pass that way safely because Serb forces and Croat forces, anybody could be in that forest. Nobody can have safe passage there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. It seems clear that this task that -- this road that you wanted to deblockade was the only one that could be there.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this deblockade was attempted after how many requests put forth to the Croat side to deblockade the road?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I just heard that this was requested or offered or whatever several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you said in addition to this offer that what was guaranteed was that nobody would get in harm's way.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that everybody could pass down that road, that they should just be released to go down that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they should just be released and allowed to take that road.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now that you are talking about the forces around Saborsko --

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Can I just say something else? I cannot claim this, that this is exactly the way it was, what I said just now, because I did not really participate in any of this, but everybody talked about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. You were a soldier, not an officer. I fully understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, you say that you did not talk to the military. You said that awhile ago when answering questions, and you did not who was there, because you were asked about that.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you're saying. Could you please clarify what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you were asked how come the army was there, and it was the army that was there in the training facility.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So we've clarified that. And then you were asked whether the police was there, and you said that you did not see the police but that they must have been there.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How come you know that they must have been there if you did not see them?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, how do I know this? I know because people talked about it later. But I said that I was on the other side and that I could not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I understand that. So you could not see them. All right. Also, you were asked, for example, whether Ogrizovic was there too, and you answered: "Yes, certainly. I did not see him, but he must have been there." So you did not see him but you believe that he must have been there.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How come these houses were on fire? Due to the artillery fire, or did you see that somebody came and torched them intentionally?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I did not see anybody torching them but everything was on fire. Everything was on fire. All of it was set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So is it your assumption that this was due to artillery fire or had somebody intentionally torched the houses?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Both are possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Both are possible but you cannot testify about that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I cannot because I did not see anyone personally setting the houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you did not see anybody personally setting the houses on fire. You say that there were some dead on the Croat side. As far as I understood this, you heard somebody from the neighbouring detachment say this to you, that Pero Krtan got killed. And when this man said that, he cried because he had heard that this man had been killed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how come you know that anybody else was killed?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, this man said it. He said, "They killed Pero Krtan," and then he was crying. And then he said, "And two more men."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And how come you have this information? I understood it that way. I don't remember whether you said it or the other side, when they asked you; how come you had this information that 20 people were killed there?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Later on, people found out. Later on it was heard that there were about 20 dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so there were rumours to the effect that there were 20 persons who were dead.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, that's what people said. I tell you, I did not see anybody. I did not see a single casualty. I myself did not see any casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you did hear that Pero Krtan was killed.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. That is the first knowledge that this group of mine got. This is the first knowledge that we had of anybody being dead in Saborsko. Until then, we did not hear that anybody got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When you say that some old people went to bury the dead, you mentioned that an excavator was used, but you also mentioned that there were animals there that had been killed too.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So do you assume that this excavator was used, not for burying people but for interring the dead animals?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I heard that this area had to be mopped up. That's the first time I ever heard that word used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that means that the killed livestock should be buried and so on. Did you hear anything about the burial of people?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that they found some people who were dead, dismembered bodies. I heard that. This is probably due to the missiles that fell there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you heard that this Pero Krtan was killed, and they told you that two more people lost their lives.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do I infer correctly on the basis of what you've been saying that everybody who got killed got killed in the shelling? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, I would not put it that way. Pero Krtan and these two men, in my opinion, are the only ones who did not get killed during the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So how did they lose their lives?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: They were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, they were killed. Do you know who killed them? Does anybody know?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, people talk about this, who killed them, but I did not see this. People know the names of these persons who killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So names were mentioned as to who had killed them?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: See, I wonder -- I wonder about this information that you are providing. I have this statement of yours. Let me just find it, the one that you gave in Karlovac. In Karlovac. So -- it says the Republic of Croatia, Ministry of the Interior, Police Department Karlovac, criminal investigation police, anti-terrorism section, and then it says "Official Note." In that Official Note, you do not mention that these three men were killed. I assume that you do have that statement that you made, don't you? It says here: "In the direction of the attack where my company was moving, nobody was caught alive, and I also claim that I did not see a single dead body. People had probably fled and withdrawn before we came. Just as we were in Saborsko, one of our soldiers, Bogdan Cubra, came in tears and said they had killed Pero Bicanin nicknamed Krtan. And he had actually been killed by Peic and those others who were with him. I did not see this personally. I believe Cubra saw it for himself or he found Pero dead. They were close," meaning to say that they were close friends; right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Bogdan Cubra and Pero Krtan knew each other and were good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you don't know that he saw him or that he found the dead body of Pero.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: He said that that man had killed. This is what he said. And I couldn't assert this because I didn't see this myself. This is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what explanation did he give? Why did that person kill Pero Krtan?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, that's my opinion. I'm giving you my opinion. Those two or three men who were there, the way I see it, those were people who just couldn't fit into any society, and the time came when they did this. It's not that they bothered them, that Pero Krtan was a Croat, it's just that he had several thousand Deutschmarks on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're trying to say that Pero Krtan was killed for -- in an attempt to rob him.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: No, no, no. You didn't understand me. What I'm saying is that those people that, according to Bogdan Cubra killed him - you know, he said that those people killed Pero Krtan - those people killed Pero because they thought he had money, not because he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly what I said. They killed him in order to rob him, not because he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They killed him because they thought he had money.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They killed him because they wanted to rob him.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to what you said here, you didn't see anybody get killed. You heard that Pero Krtan had been killed. You believe that he had been killed because it was a robbery, and that's all you're saying.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you know that there were some 50 to 60 Croats there that were collected, taken to another village. They were given sandwiches; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then the following day, they were taken in a bus to a line where the territory under the control of the Croatian army started?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody harass them?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: No, these people were definitely not harassed by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other civilians there harassed by anybody, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other civilians, Croats, and were they harassed by anybody? Did you see anybody harass any Croat civilian?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: No, definitely not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these people were taken immediately the following day in a bus to the territory?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, to the territory held by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that some two or three people were looting a store and that they were the only ones who could have come up with that kind of an idea. Do you know those two or three men who looted that store, since you say they were the only ones capable of that? That means you must have had some preconceived notions of these people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, you are the one who mentioned these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the names out of the statement given to the police in Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these same people who killed Pero Krtan were the ones who looted the store?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, they were the only ones capable of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the reason behind this was robbery or looting again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many people are we talking about? You said two or three.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Just a couple of them. A couple. Two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A couple.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. A couple. And at that time, they were the only ones capable of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the only ones.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did anybody report them to police?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: It wasn't easy to report them. It wasn't easy for anyone to do that because they had weapons, and it was difficult to report them to anyone. They would have killed anyone. They would have killed me. They wouldn't even blink.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was a group of two or three robbers, looters.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were not JNA soldiers, were they? They were just people who you knew.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. These were people who would not put themselves under anyone's command. They had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they from your place and is that why you knew them so well?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. They were from my town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you say that after Saborsko was taken, one could travel. There was no blockades anywhere throughout the entire territory. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go back to something else. I wanted to clarify Saborsko while it's still fresh in our mind so that there is no need to go back to that unless something else comes up. Can you please tell me, is it true that in your town where you lived in 1991, according to data that I have, there were some over 2.000 Serbs and only 64 Croats.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I think that there was a far greater number of Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me how many. This is the data that I have, and I would like to know what's correct.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I think that my town, together with surrounding villages, had some 4.000 people able to vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I'm referring now just to your town, not the entire municipality and surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, yes. If you mean the town alone, then, yes, it's not a large place, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, is this figure that I gave you correct, that there were some 2.000 Serbs and 64 Croats?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: That number would be too great for the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, give us the figure. How many inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, some 4.500 to 5.000 inhabitants altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many were Serbs and how many were Croats?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I think some 2 per cent were Croats, 2 or 3 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So just 2 or 3 per cent.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the majority of people in the police station were Serbs, although there were Croats there as well, even though the percentage of Croats was only 2 or 3 per cent. But there was a portion that corresponded to the composition of the population.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I don't know what the reasons were for that type of composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you are a protected witness, I will not mention the -- the place where you worked, the company where you worked, but you said that there in the company where you worked and when you were a supervisor, that 32 people were fired, were dismissed from work. You must know what company is involved, and you also must know that the production process ceased in that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you mean to say that everybody was dismissed?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. They were sent -- a telegram came in, saying that they all had to take unpaid leave, and it was expected that it wasn't going to last long. And I was the only one who, according to the telegram, had to be on duty from 7.00 until 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And what nationality were those workers that had been dismissed?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they were dismissed for that very reason.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, for that very reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since -- when those few Croats who were in the police station in your town left, did somebody else come? When you were asked this question, you said that some new locals came who filled up the number of the needed policemen.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, they were locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they were there in charge of law and order in those settlements that were practically populated by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there still some 2 to 3 per cent of Croat inhabitants there?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they leave that territory?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. I know that actually one or two of people in the police were from Saborsko, and then later on it was impossible. I don't know if you understand this, but later on it was impossible for them to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there were roadblocks on both sides.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the Serb side, Serb forces controlled it; and on the Croat side, Croat forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did somebody force those Croats to leave that area or did they simply --

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I think that they simply saw that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They had to leave under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 on page 1 of your statement, you said that Serbs started getting concerned for their security after the referendum on the independence of Croatia was held; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said during chief examination that Professor Raskovic wanted the Serb rights to be protected and respected in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I heard that Professor Raskovic said that as long as Croatia respected Serb rights, that Serb people would respond in kind, and then at one point he said that he would use all available democratic means to enforce those rights, but he said, "If you're looking for a war leader, then I'm a wrong person," because he was not favouring the war option. At least, that's how I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. So he was right. All he wanted was to make sure that Serb people are treated equally in Croatia, equally with anyone else, and their rights were respected. He didn't want anything else.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, he didn't want anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you agreed with him, you thought that he was right; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that, otherwise, relations between Serbs and Croats were good in the area you lived but, however, they deteriorated quite fast; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because when asked here, you said that the reasons for that were contained in the fact that HDZ sent bad messages to Serb people. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And -- and what did he say?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: He said, and I read this in the paper, that he -- he addressed on Easter the population, and he said that the Serbs were a disturbing factor and as long as they were there, Croatia would not exist as a state, that Serbs need to be expelled, converted into Catholicism, and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you probably know that Ustashas had the same slogan during World War II: Kill, convert, and expel.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the same thing was repeated now again.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying. This is the message that was sent and that could be heard from various gatherings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was Sime Djodan who sent this message?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: He was an MP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this was the message or the speech he gave in Croatian Assembly, parliament?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was in various gatherings, and I saw this in the papers. I read this in the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You read it in Vecernji List, an evening daily in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, were you informed that specifically for these -- because of these events, the Presidency of Yugoslavia then, in the beginning of October of 1991, declared that the country was in an immediate threat of war? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did you know something about the establishing of Croatian paramilitary in the form of Croatian National Guards, ZNG?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that, and I was surprised by that when in the stadium Maksimir in Zagreb they were promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in 1991, in the very beginning. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who did ZNG, the National Guard Corps, consist of?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the creation of the National Guard as a threat directed at Serbs?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. But all I'm saying is that the Serb people at that time lived in great fear. And as for politics, I was never interested in that. And I don't think that I would be able to give you a quality answer if this is what you're aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to ask any political questions of you. You explained that there was fear. You gave an example of Sime Djodan.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You described about how the National Guard Corps was established. And I suppose that even though this is not an especially political issue, you knew that the National Guard Corps was an illegal armed formation because, normally, there should only be the army and the police, and that's what we had in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In these events that you're describing in Saborsko that was in November of 1991, that was taking place whilst the JNA existed in the entire territory of Yugoslavia. That was prior to the recognition of Croatian independence.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that the proclamation of Independent Croatia and establishment of National Guard Corps and all of these events - don't let me go back to Djodan and other representatives of theirs - that all of that was accompanied with a great number of Ustasha symbols and various other symbols dating from World War II?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During 1991 and before the November events, so before the November events described by you, were there any armed conflicts in Croatia between these paramilitary forces of Croatia, such as National Guard Corps, ZNG, on one side and Serb people on the other side?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. There was that event in Plitvice lakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What took place there?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: There was a conflict there which broke out between Serbs and Croatian forces, and I think that was during Easter time. It was on the 1st of April. It was Catholic Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean Easter of 1991?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes. At least, that's what I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how did this conflict break out?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, they were not allowed to go to Plitvice because allegedly Serb forces were in Plitvice. And they wanted -- or they couldn't pass any more on that road, and this is why the conflict took place. And we heard that there were casualties there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people got killed then in Plitvice in that conflict?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: As far as I know, one Croatian and one Serb soldier got killed. I don't know whether it was exactly there or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn there about the events when, for example, Serb paramilitary -- Croat paramilitary formations, together with the MUP of Croatia, in the beginning of -- in November of 1991 attacked and destroyed 18 protected Serb villages in Papuk, Slunj, and neighbouring areas?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes, we heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that prior to these events described on pages 2, 3, 4 of your statements -- of your statement - I'm not going to refer to them now but you know which ones I have in mind - so is it true that these formations such as ZNG and other paramilitary formations, that they blocked and attacked dozens of barracks of the JNA in the territory of Croatia, throughout Croatia? Do you know about that? They were blocked and attacked.

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: Witness C-1220
utterances.text: Well, that's something that we were able to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we're getting a long way from the witness's evidence, a long way from what he can give evidence about realistically. Now, Mr. Milosevic, have you got very much more for this witness? It appears you've covered virtually everything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. I suppose that I have a right to continue examining him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, but you don't have to take up all the time. Mr. Tapuskovic, have you got any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will have just a few questions. I will probably finish within a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, tomorrow morning. Witness C-1220, could you be back, please, tomorrow morning, 9.00, to conclude your evidence. We will -- before we rise, we will hand in the exhibits which weren't, in the event, produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
